gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy the picks actually delivered in a named test: OutdoorGearLab measured 3,790 Wh out of the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3's 4,096 Wh, and Outdoor Life measured 2,290 Wh out of the BLUETTI Apex 300's 2,765 Wh (83%). Nor does any result put the measured idle draws side by side: Apex 300 about 20 W, F3800 Plus about 40 W, Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus about 58 W, all from The Solar Lab.
standout_why: I compared against the rival pages I could open. thesolarlab.com 'Best Big Power Stations' (cited) gives idle draw only for the F3800 Plus (about 40 W) and the Apex 300 (about 20 W, about 85% efficiency). It has no idle figure for the DELTA Pro 3 or the Jackery 5000 Plus and no measured delivered energy for any model, and it shows no author, date or method. StormWatts (cited) says 'We have not tested these products hands-on' and lists maker specs only. EnergySage (cited) says 'EnergySage did not test these models' and gives only an 80–85% rule of thumb. Neither page has measured capacity or idle draw. theoutageplan.com (self-signed certificate error), goodhousekeeping.com (fetch blocked), solargenreview.com (HTTP 429) and offsetsolar.com (not attempted) were not checked. Partly covered: the two idle figures above. New: delivered Wh for the DELTA Pro 3 and Apex 300, the Jackery idle figure, and one side-by-side table.
decides: This supports the DELTA Pro 3 as the pick for most households. OutdoorGearLab's 3,790 Wh delivered (92.5% of rated) is the best measured result among these picks, and The Solar Lab measured 89% efficiency on a sustained 3,650 W load. For a long outage with the inverter left on, idle draw changes the ranking among the rest. The Apex 300 at about 20 W uses about 0.48 kWh a day. The F3800 Plus at about 40 W uses about 0.96 kWh a day. The Jackery 5000 Plus at about 58 W uses about 1.4 kWh a day, which is roughly a fridge's daily use lost to standby. That weakens the case for the Jackery 5000 Plus that ChatGPT showed, even with its larger battery.

findings.note: Measured on OutdoorGearLab's test jig. 3,790 / 4,096 = 92.5%; the text rounds this to 'over 93%'. Same review: average charge rate 1,293 Wh/h, peak AC input about 1,600 W, full charge in 3.2 h.

findings.note: 3.7 / about 5 kWh is about 74% round trip. That is my arithmetic from the reviewer's two figures, not a figure the reviewer gives. Charging took 3 hours from 0 to 100%.

findings.label: Measured inverter efficiency and AC charge time (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 89% efficiency on a sustained 3,650 W load for 60 min; AC (120 V) charge in about 2 h 54 min vs 2 h 20 min advertised
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 review, The Solar Lab
findings.note: The page gives no author or date (only 'Copyright © 2026'). It also says the unit held 5,100 W for nearly a minute before shutting down.
